title: Reduce token variance for high-density tables and charts to improve legibility and runtime surface consistency
creator: Ava Morales
description:
Problem: Over time the token set has expanded into many close-but-distinct color/typography/spacing variants aimed at micro-optimizations for specific components. For data-dense surfaces (tables, heatmaps, small-multiples) this variance causes inconsistent contrast, shadow stacking oddities, and unpredictable perceived density across breakpoints.

Goal: Consolidate and rationalize the token ranges used for high-density components into a small, predictable set of surface tones, elevation steps, and compact type scales so engineering can reliably apply a single density profile without per-component micro-variance. Deliverables: updated token spec, Figma component kit updates, migration guide for engineers, test prompts for visual regression and accessibility checks.

Scope: color palettes for surface/row backgrounds, typography scale for compact tables/charts (12px-14px lanes), spacing/radius rules for dense controls, and shadow/elevation blending for stacked rows and chart layer overlays. Excludes global theme remapping for marketing surfaces and full redesigns of chart components themselves.

Trade-offs considered:
- Narrowing tokens reduces designer expressiveness but improves consistency and runtime predictability.
- Larger elevation steps improve layering clarity but reduce micro-depth nuance in bespoke components.

Related artifacts: Figma file (see design_links), migration checklist and PR template for engineering (see engineering_links).
acceptance_criteria: Design token spec updated and published in the design library with examples for table/row states and chart overlays
Figma components (tables, small-multiples, heatmap) updated to use consolidated tokens and reviewed by PM and Accessibility
Engineering implementation plan includes token aliasing strategy and a phased migration path (alias -> deprecation) with feature flags
Visual regression suite updated to cover compact density snapshots across 3 viewport widths and pass with no perceptible contrast regressions
Accessibility checks confirm minimum AA contrast on table text and selected chart labels for compact sizes
tasks: Audit existing tokens used by tables/charts and produce a candidate consolidation map
Define compact type scale (primary, secondary, caption) for dense surfaces
Propose 3 surface tone anchors and 2 elevation steps for dense layering
Design review with PM, Accessibility, and Engineering to finalize values
Update Figma components and publish a new component kit version
Create engineering migration doc: alias mapping, feature flag rollout, UI tests
Implement tokens in CSS/vars and expose in tokens registry (engineering owners: @eng-tokens)
Run cross-browser visual regressions and manual QA on high-density dashboards
Prepare rollout announcement and deprecation timeline
